description.value: A 28-site BC Parks campground on the Kiskatinaw River along the original Alaska Highway, anchored by a rare surviving WWII-era curved wooden trestle bridge just a short walk from camp; the warm, slow river is good for tubing though fishing is limited by murky water.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The BC Parks website for Kiskatinaw Park confirms the campground's location (28km north of Dawson Creek on the Old Alaska Highway along the Kiskatinaw River), activities, and cycling policies. OSM tags confirm capacity of 28 sites, a fee-based campground, no internet access, and operator contact details. The website's cycling section explicitly states e-bikes are not permitted on trails (restricted to park roads only), and the park page references frontcountry camping reservation policies.
concerns: OSM phone (+1-250-843-0092) and email (sandstormnorth@gmail.com) belong to the private operator Sandstorm North Contracting, not BC Parks directly; the BC Parks contact page lists different general numbers (1-800-689-9025). Phone could not be corroborated via website content.
No street address available in OSM or on the website; location is described only as '28km north of Dawson Creek off Highway 97 on the Old Alaska Highway'.
Many amenity details (potable water, showers, reservations) are not explicitly confirmed or denied on the park page and remain unknown.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A legitimate, active BC Parks provincial campground in Northern BC with 28 sites, accessible by road and relevant to touring cyclists riding the Alaska Highway corridor near Dawson Creek.
enrichment_extras.notes: E-bikes are explicitly restricted to park roads; they are not permitted on trails. This is worth flagging to e-bike touring cyclists. The campground sits on the historic original Alaska Highway route, making it of particular interest to cyclists following that corridor.
